label: phototoxic porphyria
definition: An inherited porphyria characterized by chronic blistering or non-blistering cutaneous manifestations, including photosensitivity, fragile skin, blistering, scarring, hyperpigmentation, hypertrichosis, and alopecia. These symptoms arise from the accumulation of photoreactive porphyrin precursors in circulating erythrocytes, which triggers phototoxicity primarily by damaging endothelial cells in the skin upon light exposure.

label: neurovisceral porphyria
definition: An inherited porphyria that presents as acute/episodic attacks characterized by abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, neuropathy, and neuropsychiatric symptoms, typically without cutaneous manifestations. Triggers precipitating acute attacks include estrogen/progesterone, oral contraceptives, alcohol, drugs, stress, or infections.

label: neurovisceral and phototoxic porphyria
definition: An inherited porphyria that presents with neurovisceral attacks (severe abdominal pain, vomiting, neuropathy) and photosensitivity (chronic blistering cutaneous manifestations). These symptoms arise from the accumulation of both neurotoxic ALA and photoreactive porphyrin precursors in circulating erythrocytes, which triggers phototoxicity.

label: acute hepatic porphyria
definition: A hepatic porphyria characterized by intermittent acute neurovisceral attacks caused by the accumulation of neurotoxic porphyrin precursors (primarily delta-aminolevulinic acid [ALA] and porphobilinogen [PBG]) produced mainly in the liver. This group encompasses ALAD-related neurovisceral porphyria, HMBS-related neurovisceral porphyria, CPOX-related neurovisceral and phototoxic porphyria, and PPOX-related neurovisceral and phototoxic porphyria.

label: homozygous dominant acute intermittent porphyria
definition: Acute intermittent porphyria caused by biallelic variants in HMBS inherited in an autosomal recessive inheritance pattern, and characterized by an extremely rare, predominantly neurologic presentation with childhood onset, including developmental abnormalities, ataxia, dysarthria, leukoencephalopathy, cataracts and optic nerve hypoplasia.

label: SETBP1-related neurodevelopmental disorder
definition: Any neurodevelopmental disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the SETBP1 gene. Variants in SETBP1 are associated with three different phenotypes: Schinzel-Giedion midface retraction syndrome, SETBP1 haploinsufficiency disorder, and SETBP1-related neurodevelopemental disorder caused by missense variant of unknown functional effect.

label: SETBP1-related neurodevelopemental disorder caused by missense variant of unknown functional effect
definition: A neurodevelopmental disorder caused by a pathogenic missense variant of unknown functional effect that are not within or adjacent to the mutational hot spot in the SETBP1 gene. It is characterized by intellectual disability or developmental delay, speech and language delay, hypotonia and sleep issues, with variable seizures, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and autistic traits, and a greater risk of orthopedic, gastrointestinal and heart issues than SETBP1 haploinsufficiency disorder. Inheritance is autosomal dominant and usually de novo.

label: isolated congenital long QT syndrome
definition: A form of familial long QT syndrome (LQTS) characterized by syncopal episodes and electrocardiographic abnormalities (QT prolongation, T-wave abnormalities and torsade de pointes (TdP) ventricular tachycardia).

label: acquired long QT syndrome
definition: A long QT syndrome characterized by pathologic excessive prolongation of the QT interval, upon exposure to an environmental stressor, with reversion back to normal following removal of the stressor. It is most often due to specific drugs or metabolic abnormalities, such as hypokalemia or hypomagnesemia.

label: BMPR1B-related fibular hypoplasia and complex brachydactyly
definition: An autosomal recessive acromesomelic dysplasia in which the cause of the disease is a hypomorphic mutation in the BMPR1B gene. It belongs to a spectrum of skeletal dysplasias characterized by short stature, severe acromesomelic shortening of the limbs, and normal axial skeleton.

label: metastatic malignant neoplasm from the breast
definition: A metastatic malignant neoplasm that originates from a primary malignant neoplasm of the breast and has spread to a secondary site.

label: metastatic breast cancer in the liver
definition: A metastatic malignant neoplasm in the liver that originates from a primary malignant neoplasm of the breast.

label: metastatic colon cancer in the liver
definition: A metastatic malignant neoplasm in the liver that originates from a primary malignant neoplasm of the colon.

label: metastatic malignant neoplasm in the liver
definition: A malignant neoplasm that has spread to the liver from another (primary) anatomic site. Representative examples include carcinomas, lymphomas, melanomas, or sarcomas.

label: VWF-related von Willebrand disease
definition: A hereditary von Willebrand disease caused by pathogenic variation in VWF, resulting in abnormalities of von Willebrand factor quantity or function that impair hemostasis. VWF-related von Willebrand disease encompasses both quantitative deficiencies of VWF and qualitative defects affecting VWF-mediated platelet adhesion, platelet interaction, or factor VIII binding.

label: VWF-related quantitative von Willebrand disease
definition: VWF-related quantitative von Willebrand disease is characterized by decreased circulating VWF levels and impaired primary hemostasis, and includes both partial quantitative deficiency (von Willebrand disease type 1) and virtually complete quantitative deficiency (von Willebrand disease type 3).

label: VWF-related von Willebrand disease with decreased platelet tethering
definition: A VWF-related qualitative von Willebrand disease in which pathogenic variation in VWF reduces the ability of von Willebrand factor to support platelet tethering and adhesion under conditions of vascular injury.

label: epithelioid angiosarcoma
definition: Epithelioid angiosarcoma is a highly aggressive endothelial cell malignancy, most commonly arising in the deep soft tissues, but a variety of primary sites, including the adrenals, thyroid, skin, and bone, are encountered.

label: SAT1-related X-linked systemic lupus erythematosus
definition: Any systemic lupus erythematosus in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the SAT1 gene. Loss-of-function variants in SAT1 cause X-linked childhood-onset systemic lupus erythematosus.

label: DNAJC17 deficiency
definition: Any inborn error of immunity in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the DNAJC17 gene. It is characterized by retinopathy, combined immunodeficiency, and TNF-driven autoinflammation responsive to targeted TNF blockade.

label: autosomal recessive severe congenital neutropenia due to CSF3 deficiency
definition: Any autosomal recessive severe congenital neutropenia in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the CSF3 gene.

label: combined immunodeficiency due to SIT1 deficiency
definition: Any combined immunodeficiency in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the SIT1 gene.

label: SH3GL1 deficiency
definition: Any B cell deficiency in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the SH3GL1 gene.

label: CD48-related hemophagocytic syndrome
definition: Any hemophagocytic syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the CD48 gene.

label: IRAK2 deficiency
definition: Any inborn error of immunity in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the IRAK2 gene.

label: FGR-related monogenic vasculitis
definition: Any vasculitis in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the FGR gene.

label: MAGIS syndrome, GNAI2-related
definition: Any inborn error of immunity in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the GNAI2 gene. It is characterized by midline malformations of the brain, anterior pituitary gland dysfunction, growth retardation, immunodysregulation/immunodeficiency, and skeletal defects.

label: CASP1-related autoinflammatory syndrome
definition: Any autoinflammatory syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a gain-of-function variation in the CASP1 gene. It is characterized by systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis and recurrent macrophage activation syndrome, with elevated IL-1beta and IL-18, and progressive interstitial lung disease.

label: inborn error of immunity due to STXBP3 deficiency
definition: Any inborn error of immunity in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the STXBP3 gene. It is characterized by medically refractory infantile-onset IBD, bilateral sensorineural hearing loss and, in the majority, recurrent infections.

label: TBL1XR1-related disorder
definition: Any disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the TBL1XR1 gene.

label: herpes simplex encephalitis due to TMEFF1 deficiency
definition: An inherited susceptibility to acute infection-induced encephalitis in which the cause is a variation in the TMEFF1 gene, predisposing to herpes simplex encephalitis. Genetic TMEFF1 deficiency allows HSV-1 to rapidly enter cortical neurons.

label: combined immunodeficiency due to RGS10 deficiency
definition: Any combined immunodeficiency in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the RGS10 gene. It is characterized by recurrent infections, hypergammaglobulinemia, profoundly reduced lymphocyte chemotaxis, abnormal lymph node architecture, and short stature due to growth hormone deficiency.

label: combined immunodeficiency with epigenetic dysfunction, ASXL1-related
definition: Any combined immunodeficiency in which the cause of the disease is a biallelic germline mutation in the ASXL1 gene. It is characterized by progressive B-cell loss with hypogammaglobulinemia, recurrent pneumonia, progressive cytopenias,impaired cytotoxic T and NK cell populations, chronic macrocytosis, chronic ulcerated granulomatous skin lesions, and EBV-associated Hodgkin lymphoma. Genome-wide DNA methylation showed extensive hypomethylation, epigenetic age approximately 27 years older than chronological age, and shortened telomeres.

label: isolated immunodeficiency, TKFC-related
definition: Any immunodeficiency disease in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the TKFC gene. It is characterized by chronic active Epstein-Barr virus disease, multiple bacterial and viral infections, hypogammaglobulinemia, near-absent natural killer cells, and decreased memory B cells, without the multisystem features of triokinase and FMN cyclase deficiency syndrome.

label: ELP1-related medulloblastoma predisposition
definition: A hereditary neoplastic syndrome caused by germline loss-of-function variation in the ELP1 gene. It is characterized by an increased risk of childhood Sonic Hedgehog (SHH)-activated medulloblastoma.

label: ALG2-related congenital disorder of glycosylation
definition: Any congenital disorder of glycosylation in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the ALG2 gene. It includes congenital disorder of glycosylation type Ii and congenital myasthenic syndrome 14.

label: PTPN1-related type 1 interferonopathy
definition: Any type 1 interferonopathy in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the PTPN1 gene.

label: DROSHA-related tumor predisposition
definition: Hereditary tumor predisposition due to variation(s) in the DROSHA gene. Pathogenic germline loss-of-function variants in DROSHA confer a predisposition to pineoblastoma, usually in childhood, which may be recurrent or metastatic. Wilms tumor has also been reported. Tumors carry a somatic second variation in DROSHA.

label: HSPD1-related neurologic disorder
definition: Any hereditary neurological disease in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the HSPD1 gene.
